title: Sprint retrospective
text:
Dev: Let's start with what went well this sprint.
Ines: The new deploy pipeline. We shipped four times and none of them needed a rollback.
Omar: Pairing on the import bug helped too. We found it in a day instead of a week.
Dev: Good. What did not go well?
Ines: Code review was slow. Some pull requests waited three days for a first look.
Omar: And the sprint was overloaded from the start. We took on more than we finished.
Dev: Why do you think review was slow?
Ines: Everyone was heads down on their own tickets, and nobody owned the review queue.
Omar: Maybe one person each day could be the first reviewer for anything new.
Dev: A review rotation. I like that. Ines, can you set it up for next sprint?
Ines: Yes, I will put a rotation in the team calendar.
Dev: For the overload, I think we should bring fewer tickets into planning and keep a buffer for bugs.
Omar: Twenty percent buffer would have covered this sprint's bugs.
Dev: Let's try that. So two actions: the review rotation and a buffer of twenty percent in planning.
Ines: Should we write down the pipeline win too, so we keep doing it?
Dev: Yes, I will add it to the notes. Thanks, everyone.

report.label: review rotation
quotes: A review rotation. I like that.
